title: Driving Test Prep
source: Common written driving-test topics: road signs, right-of-way, and basic traffic rules (right-hand-traffic countries such as the U.S.)

cards.prompt: In a right-hand-traffic country, a downward-pointing triangular sign with a red border and white background means the driver must:
distractors: Not enter the road at all
Slow to the posted speed limit
cards.explanation: Yield signs are triangular and stop signs are octagonal, so drivers can tell them apart by shape alone, even from an angle or when a sign face is obscured. A yield only requires stopping if traffic is actually present; a stop sign requires a full stop every time.

cards.prompt: In a right-hand-traffic country, at an all-way stop where two vehicles arrive at exactly the same time, which one has the right of way?
cards.explanation: This 'right rule' only breaks a tie. When vehicles do not arrive simultaneously, the vehicle that stopped first goes first regardless of position; the right-of-vehicle rule applies only when arrival order is otherwise ambiguous.

cards.prompt: On a two-way road, what does a solid yellow line on your side of the center line mean?
cards.answer: Passing (overtaking) is not allowed from your side of the road.
cards.explanation: The rule is about sight distance and oncoming risk, not the line itself: a solid line marks a stretch where a driver cannot reliably see far enough ahead to pass safely, such as a curve or hill crest. A broken yellow line on your side means passing is allowed when the way ahead is clear.

cards.prompt: On most road signs, a red circle with a diagonal line through a symbol means that action is {{prohibited}}.
cards.explanation: This red-circle-and-slash convention comes from the Vienna Convention on Road Signs and Signals, which is why it looks similar across many countries even when the language on other signs differs.

cards.prompt: In the U.S., what color are warning signs for general hazards such as sharp curves or falling rocks?
cards.explanation: Orange is reserved for temporary construction and work-zone signs, so a driver can immediately tell a permanent road hazard (yellow) from a temporary one (orange) without reading the sign's text.

cards.prompt: On a two-lane road, what must a driver do when approaching a school bus that has flashing red lights and an extended stop arm?
cards.answer: Stop completely and wait until the lights stop flashing and the stop arm is withdrawn, regardless of direction of travel.
cards.explanation: This rule applies to traffic in both directions on an undivided road because children may cross from either side unpredictably; it is one of the few stop requirements that ignores which lane you are in.

cards.prompt: Between two lanes moving in the same direction, what does a dashed (broken) white line indicate?
cards.answer: Lane changes are permitted when it is safe to do so.
distractors: Only buses may use this lane.
cards.explanation: A solid white line between same-direction lanes carries the opposite meaning: it discourages or restricts lane changes, often near exits or lane drops, so the dashed line is the more common default between ordinary through lanes.

cards.prompt: A speed limit sign showing a number inside a white rectangle with a red border indicates the {{maximum}} speed allowed under normal conditions.
cards.explanation: A separate black-on-white 'minimum speed' sign, without a red border, sets a floor rather than a ceiling; the two sign types are easy to confuse if a driver only looks at the number and not the border and wording.

cards.prompt: In the U.S., what shape is a stop sign, chosen so it can still be recognized even when its colors have faded?
cards.explanation: The unique octagon shape lets drivers recognize a stop sign by its outline alone, even from behind, at night with weak headlight illumination, or when the red paint has faded to nearly white.

cards.prompt: What must a driver do at an intersection controlled by a flashing red traffic light?
cards.answer: Come to a complete stop, then proceed when it is safe, exactly as at a stop sign.
distractors: Slow down but continue through without stopping.
Treat it the same as a flashing yellow light and proceed with caution.
Stop only if cross-traffic is visible.
cards.explanation: A flashing red light is legally equivalent to a stop sign, requiring a full stop every time. A flashing yellow light is a different, weaker instruction: it means slow down and proceed with caution, without a mandatory stop.
